If an actual negative classical u has compact strict negative sublevels on the stated Laurent domain, logarithmic attenuation and barrier gluing produce a potential with exactly the same poles, canonical no loss, finite global top mass and every positive power energy. The representative has exponential capacity tails and can match −log(1−u)−ε near a prescribed compact set. This does not identify every polar set with a complete pole set.

On the original q-dimensional unit polydisc with S=[V], g_T=−min(t,T), t=−log max_i|T_i|, has bounded top current δ_{σ(T)}. Scaling gives explicit energy and capacity formulas. As T tends to infinity, the Gauss points σ(T) tend to the rational origin on all original compact scalar tests.

Use the exact original q-dimensional polydisc background S=[V] and its Gauss shell calibration, with q≥1. For the continuity example fix s>0 and set u_T=T^(−s/(q+s))g_T, so e_s(u_T)=1. For the recursive example take the unbounded logarithmic pole u=log max_i|T_i|; its lower multipliers are coefficient-integrable, but it has persistent truncation loss. The scaled shell has critical weighted mass exactly one at σ(T), while local truncated gap capacities tend to zero; this leaves a Dirac limit at the origin. For the logarithmic pole, bounded uncut top products tend to the same Dirac mass but every nonpolar restriction removes it. These constructions disprove the proposed weaker hypotheses; they do not contradict strong critical continuity, strict subcritical continuity, or the no-loss recursion.

The normalized shell potentials have e_s=1 and converge to zero in full local truncated capacity, while their critical weighted currents converge to the Dirac mass at the origin. Separately, the logarithmic pole has an integrable lower-current multiplier but D(uN_{q−1})=δ_o and nonpolar top product zero. Thus same-power bounds do not replace strong or uniform-tail control, and multiplier integrability does not replace no loss.

A nonempty family in the completed cone has a relative least upper bound selected by an increasing sequence of finite maxima. Borel upper bounds and a common lower source inequality pass to this envelope. This constructs the greatest cone minorant P(f) for every f∈D_S, with energy-root and curvature estimates. The construction is relative; it supplies neither ambient upper-semicontinuous regularization nor automatic contact orthogonality.

For a fixed actual first-energy lower barrier a and finite positive Radon μ that ignores relative outer-capacity null sets and integrates −a, the completed interval [a,0] has a unique maximizer of the functional −e(v)/(q+1)−∫v dμ. Its Euler variational inequality characterizes maximality. The inequality does not assert the unrestricted source equation.

In a two-dimensional original torus with q=1, explicit bounded actual obstacles and one smooth strongly positive background violate e(P(U,V))≤e(U)+e(V). The uniform binary coefficient 2 is sharp across the specified background class. This does not make 2 sharp for every fixed S and does not refute literal strong continuity or mixed-energy Hölder constant one.

In the specified smooth torus model with 1≤q<r, canonical convex-trace evaluation is strongly continuous but is not literal integration on relative Borel classes. Literal positive data can converge in dual norm to this nonliteral functional when domination constants are not uniform. In a different radial-mixture background with n>q, an energy-bounded strongly convergent row has no Banach-weak convergent subnet. These examples preserve the fixed-domination closure theorem and closedness of the source image.

For an explicitly conormal background R and an actual parameter map s, the new potentials h_c=ψc(s) form a complete L^(k+1)_+(θ) cone, θ=s_*((-ψ)(Dψ)^k∧R). Their mixed currents and energies have exact coefficient-product formulas. This is a new parameter completion with its own boundary interpretation; it is not an identification with the full ambient classical or strong cone.

Keep the same conormal R, probe ψ, parameter measure θ and new parameter cone; put d=k+1. For the source inverse require b≥0 in L^(d/k)(θ), with datum b(s)ω. For its capacity use only h_c=ψc(s), c≥0, ||c||_(L^d)≤1; on compact cores the conditional density g_A=d s_*(1_Aω)/dθ is bounded. The exact coefficient formula makes c↦c^k the source map, so c=b^(1/k) gives the inverse and Young equality gives uniqueness within this cone. Hölder duality gives the capacity formula ||g_A||_(L^d); Radon approximation proves local regularity. These conclusions use the printed tester family and do not identify it with full normalized classical capacity.

For b≥0 in L^((k+1)/k)(θ), h=ψb(s)^(1/k) solves μ_h=b(s)(Dψ)^k∧R uniquely within the parameter cone. Its energy-normalized capacity equals the L^(k+1)(θ) norm of the conditional source density, has local regularity, and has the null ideal of its fixed source measure. The tester family is explicitly different from full classical [0,1] testers.

For the counterexample choose the allowed torus-box background R=[Y], where Y is the q-dimensional coordinate subtorus and n≥q≥1. Use the full original [0,1] tester h_a=(2L)⁻¹ max_i|t_i−a_i| at every Gauss point x_a; its top measure is L^(−q)δ_(x_a). To compare with parameter energy capacity choose the empty parameter tuple and any countable family of allowed probes. The fixed compact Gauss set is uncountable, while countably many Radon measures have only countably many atoms there. Choose a missed point; its full capacity remains at least L^(−q). The exact parameter null-ideal formula makes the same singleton null for each chosen energy capacity. This proves strict separation of the capacities without invalidating the single-probe normal-defect criterion.

For the fixed radial-mixture background of (PO3), nonnegative data with open tail H_ν(t) and nonincreasing e^tH_ν(t) admit the explicit slope A=(e^tH_ν)^(1/q), provided the stated weighted energy integral is finite. The resulting actual potential has no loss and solves the full original source equation. It is unique in the full completed cone; the necessity of the flux condition is asserted for the radial class.

For the allowed coordinate-subtorus background R=[Y] in every n≥q≥1, uncountably many Gauss singletons have uniformly positive full tester capacity. Any countable family of Radon measures misses at least one such singleton. Parameter energy capacities therefore cannot be substituted for full BT capacity. This does not obstruct the single geometry probe for normal defects, test-stage cofinality, or Choquet regularity.

On a real ball, a bounded right inverse E of normal trace gives P=I−ET from the zero-Dirichlet C^(2,α) space to functions with both boundary traces zero. The Dirichlet inverse yields K and the projection Π onto the clamped Laplacian range. Its complement Q is harmonic, and all harmonic moments characterize the linear range. The infinite-dimensional range condition is explicit.

Use 0<α<1, a real ball and the fixed original torus background S=β^(n−q)[X] with 2≤q≤n; the known negative reference is quadratic on a larger protected neighborhood. Let C₁=binom(n−1,q−1), N(h)=σ_q(I+D²h)−binom(n,q)−C₁Δh, and choose the small radius so ||K||Lip(N)/C₁≤1/2. Take g in the clamped linear range with the stated norm budget, retain small Hessians and impose a separate bound by half the negative reference margin. The projected contraction solves for h without assuming that the full nonlinear residual belongs to the linear range. Applying the Laplacian yields the exact graph f=g+QN(h(g)). Both zero traces make the extension C¹,¹ without sphere mass. Local convex smoothing, bounded Hessian convergence and the original BT continuity estimate transfer the equality to every original test.

For a nonquadratic reference fix a known C^(2,α) profile v with D²v≥cI on the protected ball, the corresponding uniformly elliptic Dirichlet inverse, and its own clamped projections K_v,Π_v,Q_v. Choose small bulk parameter g in the clamped range and prescribed ψ≤0 in C^(1,α) on the sphere; the boundary lift and contraction satisfy the printed common norm and negativity budgets. The explicit inversion from a prescribed C^(1,α) sphere density is claimed only for the quadratic reference; general C^(2,α) tangential coefficients need not have that regularity. Replace the zero normal trace by Eψ and run the projected contraction for the specified reference. Convex gluing creates the positive normal Hessian jump; a boundary-layer argument gives the exact integral sphere density rather than discarding the interface mass. The full original source has the factor q!(n−q)! on both bulk and sphere terms. A larger anchor controls both signs of fixed-interface variations in the additive ideal.

For the fixed torus background S=β^(n−q)[X], 2≤q≤n, and a protected quadratic reference, the contraction h=C₁⁻¹K(g−N(h)) gives small source data f=g+QN(h(g)). The exact local condition is Qf=QN(h(Πf)). Zero extension adds no sphere mass because both traces vanish. The resulting bounded actual potentials satisfy the source identity on every original test, with a separate negativity budget.

To go beyond the specified toric smooth backgrounds, identify an original linearized range with its boundary and moment constraints for the proposed new reference. Prove a bounded right inverse and estimates preserving that range under the nonlinear remainder; where interfaces occur, derive their original source measures and matching conditions. Verify literal strong continuity and zero normal defect for the resulting input class; the existing model graphs do not make these universal. The constructive graphs show how an explicit complemented range and controlled boundary terms can produce compatible data. Extending their method requires these new range, inverse and interface theorems. The model existence statements do not settle general SOURCE-COMPAT or permit silently adding sphere mass to an unchanged datum.

For a specified strictly convex reference, small bulk parameters and a prescribed nonpositive C^(1,α) normal trace produce actual source data with an explicit positive sphere term. The density is ∫_ψ^0 σ_(q−1)(A_T+(s/R)I_T) ds. A quadratic reference also permits explicit inversion of a small nonnegative sphere density. General C^(2,α) references permit prescribed trace; the stronger surface-density regularity is not automatic. A fixed interface admits a common enlarged additive ideal.

With q=1 in a fixed smooth torus background and n≥2, moving-sphere potentials converge uniformly and strongly while distinct radii remain separated in the full energy-difference norm. They yield an energy-difference-bounded positive cone functional that is neither strong-continuous nor literal Radon integration. An uncountable family of sphere interfaces also admits no single common principal ideal. None is a counterexample for literal positive Radon data.

Use the established R6 input: every actual delta-form of total bidegree (1,1) acts on every allowed background S of degree p<n, intrinsically on all original tests. Its agreement with PS multiplication and the full PS Leibniz rule give M_S(d′β)=d′(β∧S) and M_S(d″γ)=d″(γ∧S). This is an available input, not an additional open conjecture or a higher-degree arbitrary-current product.
